$comment: Written against a `git archive` snapshot of lablab-harness at 8a674f5.
Grading is by citation, not by prose: each read task names `want`, a
substring of one real source line, and eval/verify.mjs resolves the path:line
the agent cited and reads that line out of the snapshot. An answer can only
pass by pointing at the code.
The single-file lookups came first and are kept, because they are the
control. The multi-step ones are the point: this repository defines OUT in
6 modules and BASE in 19, so answering them means enumerating candidates and
then choosing, not hitting the right file first try.
Every want below was read out of the snapshot with sed before it was written
here. Re-check with: git archive | tar -x && grep -n

tasks.task: In this repository one module builds a result object containing a boolean field named pass. Report the exact file path and line number where that field is assigned, and quote the line. Do not modify any files.

tasks.$comment: Six modules define OUT at module level. The agent has to see all six to pick the one whose value is the weekly plan.
tasks.task: Six modules in agent/ each define a module-level constant OUT pointing at a different output file. Which one of them points at work/plan-week.md? Report the file and the line. Do not modify any files.

tasks.$comment: judge.py has two real submit gates: line 345 rejects total < 5 with a hard failure, line 348 rejects total < 7 asking for a FIX. An earlier wording of this task said 'the comparison that rejects a too-low total' and a kit-off run cited line 345, which is a correct answer, and was scored wrong. Naming the threshold removes the ambiguity without naming the file.
tasks.task: One module refuses to submit an entry and prints a message asking for a FIX before doing so. It has two such guards; report the one whose threshold is 7. Report the file, the line number and quote the comparison. Do not modify any files.

tasks.$comment: Needs two different files: research.py:20 for the output, research.py:21 for the skills path. want matches the second line.
tasks.task: One module writes its findings to work/winners.md and reads its playbooks from the user's OpenCode skills directory rather than from the repository. Report both line numbers in that module, and quote the line that builds the skills path. Do not modify any files.

tasks.$comment: Two modules define SKILLS as a list of skill names and one defines it as a Path. A grep for SKILLS returns three hits, and only one of them is the path the task asks about. Premise checked with premises.mjs: the two list definitions are byte-identical, so the agent cannot tell them apart by content and has to read which variable each module goes on to use.
tasks.task: Three modules define a module-level name SKILLS. In two of them it is a list of skill names; in one it is a Path built from the user's home directory. Report the file and line of the one that is a Path, and quote that line. Do not modify any files.

tasks.$comment: Six profiles, and four of them share the same weights dict. An agent that reads the first profile and assumes the rest match is wrong twice over. The task cannot be answered by grepping one line: the answer requires comparing six dicts and finding which two differ. Premise verified by hand: 20/20/40/20 appears four times, and the two outliers are 20/15/40/25 and 25/25/30/20, so 'Business Value: 15' and 'Technology: 30' each occur exactly once in the file.
tasks.task: One module defines six stack profiles. Four of the six have identical weights dictionaries. The other two differ from the majority. Report both outliers: the profile name and the exact weights line for each, quoting them. Do not modify any files.

tasks.$comment: The first task that needs the kit to do work rather than to shortcut it. Graded on the file after the run, not on what the agent says it did. mustNotContain is as important as mustContain: appending the new path without removing the old one is not the change that was asked for.
tasks.task: In agent/portfolio.py the weekly plan is written to work/plan-week.md. Change it so it is written to work/plan-week-v2.md instead. Make no other changes and do not reformat anything.

tasks.$comment: The first task that is real work rather than a shortcut: six profiles, six edits, and an agent that stops after the first two is the obvious failure. mustContainMin counts occurrences, because a plain substring check passes that. An earlier version of this task said the weights sum to 100 and asked for a compensating cut. That premise was false, the sums were 85/80/75 and not 100, so all four agents correctly preserved sums that were never 100 and the grader passed them anyway. A grader that only counts 'Robustness' occurrences cannot tell that difference, which is the whole reason eval/premises.mjs and the prose premise in the task text both have to be right. Premise for the current wording re-verified against lablab-harness@8a674f5: six profiles in STACK_OVERRIDE, each with a four-dimension weights dict, so adding a fifth is correct, and the fallback dict at the bottom of the file has four dimensions too and must be left alone.
tasks.task: In agent/rubric.py the STACK_OVERRIDE dict defines six stack profiles, and each profile's weights dictionary has four dimensions. Add a fifth dimension named Robustness with weight 10 to every one of those six profile dictionaries, so each profile has five dimensions. Leave the fallback dictionary at the bottom of the file alone. Make no other changes and do not reformat anything.
